claim: The sample demo searches bundled metadata across three separate vaults.
where: Demo route and landing-page first action
sandbox: Fresh browser context at /?demo=1; assert the prefilled acme search shows both Work.kdbx entries and ownership.

claim: Demo records use a separate browser-storage namespace and are discarded when starting for real.
sandbox: Fresh browser context with a sentinel real-data key; enter /?demo=1; assert only demo:vault-cross-search:* is written; choose Start for real.

claim: Reset demo restores the bundled sample data and clears the sample search.
sandbox: Fresh browser context at /?demo=1; search one known record; activate Reset demo; assert six bundled records return.

claim: The complete sample-demo flow sends no third-party requests.
sandbox: Fresh browser context at /?demo=1; record all requests during search, reset, and Start for real; allow only the local site origin.

claim: The sample demo uses bundled records without opening a file picker or calling the desktop app.
sandbox: Fresh browser context at /?demo=1 with instrumented file-picker and Tauri bridge functions; search and reset; assert no native call and no file input.

claim: After a visitor chooses Download the desktop app, the landing page asks GitHub for the latest macOS, Windows, or Linux release.
where: Landing-page download action and note, privacy policy, README
sandbox: Fresh browser contexts with macOS, Windows, and Linux user agents; intercept the GitHub API and release assets; assert no cold-load request, one request after the explicit action, and the matching platform asset.

claim: The website and policy pages load no third-party scripts, fonts, trackers, advertising, or other resources.
sandbox: Fresh browser context; record requests across home, privacy, and terms; assert every request is same-origin.

claim: Website Copy install command buttons place only their displayed public command on the clipboard after an explicit click.
where: Landing install section and privacy policy
sandbox: Fresh browser context with an instrumented clipboard; assert no write on load, click the first Copy install command button, and assert the sole write exactly equals its visible command.

claim: The hero artwork was generated for this product.
sandbox: Inspect the original image and both prompt sidecars, assert the dated provenance in the visual thesis, load the rendered 1280×853 hero, and verify its AVIF and WebP sources.

claim: The desktop index includes title, username, URL, and group path, not passwords, notes, attachments, or custom protected fields.
sandbox: In-memory KeePass group containing every allowed field plus protected password, note, attachment bytes, and custom protected data; serialize and assert exact keys and values.

claim: The desktop core unlocks a KDBX 4 vault and extracts its searchable metadata.
sandbox: Generate a KDBX 4 vault in memory, save it with a fixture password, reopen it, and assert its title, username, and group metadata.

claim: The desktop core unlocks KDBX 4 vaults with an optional key file and recovers after a wrong or missing key file.
sandbox: Generate a KDBX 4 vault protected by a password and key-file fixture; reject a different key and a missing file; then unlock with the matching key and assert indexed metadata.

claim: The Rust core clears its owned master-password buffer immediately after deriving the database key.
sandbox: Owned password string passed to the same key-derivation helper used by unlock_vault; assert its visible length is zero immediately after derivation.

claim: The unlocked vault object is consumed during metadata extraction and is not retained in the session.
sandbox: In-memory decrypted database with a protected secret; move it into extraction and assert the retained session value contains metadata but no database-only secret.

claim: The metadata index has no disk-persistence path and exists only in the current process session.
sandbox: Inspect the compiled Rust core boundary for write/create paths, populate the in-memory session, clear it, and assert no entries remain.

claim: Lock all clears every populated desktop-session index.
where: Landing page, app UI, privacy policy, README
sandbox: Populated in-memory session; invoke clear; assert the vault list and activity timestamp are empty.

claim: Locking one vault clears that vault while leaving other unlocked vaults available.
where: Landing page, app UI, privacy policy, README
sandbox: Two-vault in-memory session; lock the first and assert only the second remains, then lock the second and assert the timestamp is cleared.

claim: The desktop app clears a populated session after 15 minutes of inactivity.
where: Landing-page product facts and privacy policy
sandbox: Populated in-memory session with activity time exactly one timeout ago; expire it and assert no vaults or activity timestamp remain.

claim: Quitting the desktop app clears the populated session before exit.
sandbox: Populated in-memory session; invoke the exit cleanup used by Tauri RunEvent handling; assert no vaults or timestamp remain.

claim: Opening a result sends the owning vault path to the operating system's registered password app.
sandbox: Populated session with one indexed entry; invoke open through a recording opener; assert the owning .kdbx path is passed.

claim: The desktop binary embeds a readable fake KDBX sample vault with two searchable records.
where: Desktop first-run screen, landing walkthrough, README, and demo documentation
sandbox: Open the compile-time bundled KDBX with its non-secret sample key, assert both fake Acme metadata records, load it into an empty in-memory session, reject mixing it with an existing session, then clear it.

claim: The Tauri first-run screen has Load sample project and searches the bundled fake vault in an isolated session.
where: Desktop first-run screen, landing walkthrough, README, and demo documentation
sandbox: Fresh fixture-backed desktop window begins locked; activate Load sample project; assert the production UI renders its walkthrough, prefilled acme query, two owned results, and Sample vault.kdbx session row.

claim: Normal desktop use makes no analytics, telemetry, advertising, crash-reporting, or background-sync request.
sandbox: Fresh fixture-backed desktop webview; record requests while loading, changing theme, opening and closing license controls, searching, moving through results, and opening one; assert no request leaves the local app origin.

claim: Ctrl or Command K focuses desktop search, arrow keys move through results, and Enter opens the selected result.
sandbox: Fixture-backed desktop webview with one unlocked vault and two results; use only keyboard commands and assert the second result's vault and entry identifiers reach the production open command.

claim: The desktop app searches metadata across every unlocked vault and opens the selected result's owning vault.
where: Landing headline, desktop ready state, and README
sandbox: Fixture-backed desktop webview with unlocked Work.kdbx and Personal.kdbx vaults; search acme; assert results from both owners, select Personal with ArrowDown, and assert Enter sends its vault and entry identifiers to the production open command.

claim: The desktop app never copies secret values, autofills, or stores passwords.
sandbox: Inspect the shipped desktop UI and Rust core boundaries for clipboard, autofill, local password storage, and file-write APIs.

claim: The product has no path to upload, recover, or synchronize vault contents.
sandbox: Inspect the shipped Rust core and desktop network boundary; assert vault access is read-only and the only fetch is explicit license verification.

claim: The free edition accepts at most two simultaneous vaults.
where: Landing pricing, app UI, terms, README
sandbox: Evaluate the production vault-count policy at zero, one, and two current vaults in free state.

claim: A valid license removes the two-vault UI limit; checking, invalid, and offline-invalid states do not.
where: Landing pricing, app UI, terms, README
sandbox: Evaluate the production vault-count policy at 25 vaults for every license state.

claim: A license changes the vault-count gate, not accessibility controls, session locking, or metadata privacy.
sandbox: Fresh free and licensed webview contexts; compare controls, run axe, and assert the Rust safety core contains no license branch.

claim: After explicit license verification, only the token, verdict, and check time are stored in local webview storage.
where: Privacy policy and app license dialog
sandbox: Intercept the billing verification request with a valid fixture response; assert the cleaned URL and local token, verdict, and numeric check time.

claim: A revoked license returns the app to the free two-vault limit.
sandbox: Start with a stale valid fixture, intercept verification as revoked, and assert the cached verdict is false and the UI shows Free · 2 vaults.

claim: A previously valid cached license remains active when daily verification cannot run offline.
sandbox: Start offline with a stale valid cached fixture, abort the verification request, and assert the app still shows Licensed · unlimited.

claim: The planned unlimited-vault license is $19 once with no subscription, and purchases are not open yet.
where: Landing pricing, desktop license dialog, terms, and README
sandbox: Open the landing pricing section, desktop license dialog, terms, and README; assert exact price, no-subscription and unavailable states, plus absence of checkout links.

claim: Release manifests publish a SHA-256 for every platform installer, and the one-line installers verify it before installing.
sandbox: Generate six release assets from original filenames containing spaces; normalize final upload names, run sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS, assert every published checksum, run the Linux installer against matching and mismatched local fixtures, and inspect the Windows verification-before-launch boundary and release upload workflow.

claim: The installers are not signed by a verified publisher.
sandbox: Inspect the release workflow for absent Apple and Windows signing configuration and assert the exact disclosure on the landing page and in README.
